items.title: Virginia Beach Open: Schupp, Martinez Vich and Sewing win first titles; Goins and Fahey take gold
items.desc: Recap of the 2026 PPA Virginia Beach Open. Elliott Schupp, Jaume Martinez Vich and Sofia Sewing won their first PPA titles. John Lucian Goins won his third singles title without dropping a game. Kate Fahey took double gold.
items.body:
The 2026 Mojo Energy Pouches Virginia Beach Open ended on Sunday, Oct. 18. The first-time champions were Elliott Schupp, Jaume Martinez Vich and Sofia Sewing. John Lucian Goins won men's singles for his third PPA Tour singles title, and he did not drop a game. The PPA Tour Open, a 1,000-point event, ran Oct. 12-18 at Pickleball Virginia Beach, according to the PPA Tour event page. Several of the tour's biggest names, including Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns, were not in the draw, The Dink reported.

Schupp and Martinez Vich break through

Elliott Schupp and Jaume Martinez Vich won men's doubles in their first tournament as partners. The No. 7 seeds beat No. 3 seeds Noe Khlif and Riley Newman 11-4, 4-11, 11-4 in the final, and it was the first career PPA Tour title for both players, according to The Dink. It was also Schupp's first PPA Tour final. Martinez Vich had reached 10 PPA Tour finals before without winning one, The Dink reported. The Kitchen called it his 11th final appearance.

On the way, the pair beat No. 2 seeds Andrei Daescu and Will Howells 11-6, 11-7 in the semifinals, The Dink reported.

Goins wins singles without dropping a game

John Lucian Goins, the No. 5 seed, won men's singles by beating Martinez Vich 11-5, 11-3 in the final. That kept Martinez Vich from a second title on the day. Goins went the whole event without dropping a game, winning six matches. It was his third career PPA Tour singles title, his first since 2025, and not a first-time championship, The Dink reported. His PPA Tour profile lists him as 18 years old, based in Bradenton, Florida, and turning pro in 2024.

Before the final, Goins beat George Rangelov 11-1, 11-3 in the quarterfinals and No. 2 seed Noe Khlif 13-11, 11-1 in the semifinals, Pickleball Surge reported.

Fahey takes singles and mixed

Kate Fahey was the only player to win two events. The top seed in women's singles beat No. 21 seed Helena Jansen Fink 11-1, 11-9 in the final, the PPA Tour posted on X. She reached that final on a walkover after No. 4 seed Chao Yi Wang withdrew, Pickleball Surge reported.

In mixed doubles, Fahey played with Eric Oncins for the first time. They beat Catherine Parenteau and Riley Newman 11-13, 11-4, 11-9, coming back from 2-8 down in the third game. It was the first time she won two events at one tournament, and Oncins' second career mixed doubles title, The Kitchen reported.

Sofia Sewing was the third first-time champion. She and Parenteau beat Alix Truong and Layne Sleeth 11-8, 11-6 for the women's doubles title, Sewing's first PPA Tour title, The Dink reported.

The upsets

Martinez Vich knocked out top seed Roscoe Bellamy 11-2, 11-7 in the men's singles quarterfinals. The PPA Tour posted the result and called it "a statement win." Bellamy had arrived as the singles champion from the Chicago Cup, The Dink noted.

In men's doubles, Max Freeman and Jonathan Truong beat No. 1 seeds Eric Oncins and CJ Klinger 2-11, 11-6, 11-6 in the quarterfinals on Friday, Oct. 16, Pickleball Surge reported. Khlif and Newman then stopped Freeman and Truong on their way to the final.

Rain on Saturday

Rain on Saturday, Oct. 17, pushed back the schedule. In its first update, the PPA Tour said amateur play was postponed two hours and pro play would start no earlier than 1 p.m. EDT. Later updates moved the start to 4 p.m. EDT and then 6 p.m. ET.

The singles and mixed semifinals finished late Saturday night into early Sunday. The men's and women's doubles semifinals moved to Sunday morning, at 8 a.m. ET for women's doubles and 9 a.m. ET for men's doubles, Pickleball Surge reported. The tour's Sunday schedule post listed semifinals on PickleballTV at 8 a.m. ET, with finals at 10 a.m. ET and Tennis Channel coverage from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. ET. Yahoo Sports contributor Todd Boss described a "rough Saturday of rain" followed by fine weather for the finals.

Final results

  • Men's singles: John Lucian Goins def. Jaume Martinez Vich 11-5, 11-3
  • Women's singles: Kate Fahey def. Helena Jansen Fink 11-1, 11-9
  • Men's doubles: Elliott Schupp/Jaume Martinez Vich def. Noe Khlif/Riley Newman 11-4, 4-11, 11-4
  • Women's doubles: Catherine Parenteau/Sofia Sewing def. Alix Truong/Layne Sleeth 11-8, 11-6
  • Mixed doubles: Kate Fahey/Eric Oncins def. Catherine Parenteau/Riley Newman 11-13, 11-4, 11-9

Scores as reported by The Dink, The Kitchen and the PPA Tour on X.

items.title: The Picklr's Chapter 11, explained: what it means for members and clubs
items.desc: What Picklr Inc.'s Chapter 11 filing means for members: the timeline, first-day orders, Nov. 6 schedules deadline, the Dec. 18 claims deadline for Picklr, Inc., the Dec. 21 bar date on the Picklr Clubs Inc. docket, the DIP loan, and the clubs named in coverage.
items.body:
Picklr, Inc., the parent company of The Picklr indoor pickleball chain, is in Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The company says its clubs are still open. Below is what the court record and news reports say so far, and what it may mean for members.

Who filed, and when

Picklr, Inc. filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition on Oct. 9, 2026, in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas (Case No. 26-34687), and its subsidiary Picklr Clubs Inc. filed on Oct. 10 (Case No. 26-34690), according to the first-day declaration of chief restructuring officer Rick Rosenbloom. Both chose Subchapter V, a faster track for small businesses. The franchising subsidiary, Picklr Franchise Inc., did not file, the declaration says. The docket lists Judge Scott W. Everett.

The declaration says the company runs or franchises about 90 clubs, with nine company-operated clubs and 81 franchised clubs in about 32 states. It says the company serves about 35,000 members and that the franchised clubs are owned and run by about 77 franchisee groups.

Why the company says it filed

Founder and CEO Jorge Barragan told Sports Business Journal that the company had guaranteed lease payments for some early franchisees, about 40 locations in all, and that those guarantees became too heavy for the parent company. "We signed, unfortunately, too many corporate guarantees that landed on the holding company. And that's on us. I own it," he told SBJ.

What the CEO has said about closures

SBJ reported that no locations will close as a direct result of the filing, though Barragan expects the network to shrink. "Our goal is just to make sure that over the next 18 months to two years, as we start to see the shakeout happen, that we position our franchisees in the best position," he said. In the company's release, as quoted by WTHR, Barragan said: "Our clubs are open, and our members are playing."

What it means for members

IAPPF, a trade group for pickleball facilities, reported that a letter to members said courts, hours, schedules and memberships continue as usual, and that the company promised to contact members directly if anything changes at their club. IAPPF also pointed out that a parent company's bankruptcy does not automatically close an independently owned club, and that members should look to their local operator for details. The CRO's declaration says the first-day relief "allows the clubs to remain open and the member experience to continue without interruption."

Timeline

  • Oct. 9-10: Picklr, Inc. and Picklr Clubs Inc. file (declaration).
  • Oct. 19: The judge held the first-day hearing. Orders entered that day allow the two cases to be handled together, let the company pay employee wages and benefits, and give it until Nov. 6 to file its schedules and statement of financial affairs (claims agent documents).
  • Oct. 20: An order lets the company keep using its bank accounts and cash management system. A scheduling order sets a status conference for Nov. 24 and a Subchapter V plan deadline of Jan. 7, 2027 (docket).
  • Nov. 18: Meeting of creditors for both cases (docket).
  • Claims deadlines: Dec. 18, 2026, for claims against Picklr, Inc. The cited Picklr Clubs Inc. docket lists a separate claims deadline of Dec. 21, 2026, in the case header and in the meeting-of-creditors notice (Dkt. 8). Government claims against Picklr, Inc. are due April 7, 2027.

The financing

An investor group called Dynamus Alliance, led by franchisee Tom Neale, would sponsor the reorganization. The reported size of its commitment varies. The company's release said $4.5 million (IAPPF, WTHR), while SBJ and the St. Louis Business Journal reported $4.8 million. The amended proposed interim DIP order filed Oct. 19 describes a loan of up to $4,365,000. That total is $3,510,000 in new money, of which up to $900,000 could be borrowed on an interim basis, plus $855,000 from an earlier bridge loan. As of the docket entries through Oct. 20 listed by the claims agent, no DIP financing order had been entered.

Clubs named in coverage

  • Fair Lawn, N.J.: Expected to stay open, according to NorthJersey.com. News 12 New Jersey reported that the company said Fair Lawn is still open for play.
  • Cherry Creek South (Denver): The pause at this unopened club is a franchisee lease issue. The Denver Business Journal reported that the franchisee, Colorado Pickleball, is trying to get out of the lease and that a lawsuit complaint has been filed. The franchisee says the pause is unrelated to the parent company's bankruptcy.
  • Greenwood, Ind.: A new club planned for late 2026 at 8921 U.S. Highway 31 South. Presale for Founder Memberships began Oct. 21, WTHR reported. The local operator is Pickle Indy, LLC.
  • Burlington, Danvers, Exton, Newark and Westbrook: These locations are tied to a separate franchisee bankruptcy that 3 Strand Holdings LLC and related entities filed Sept. 24 in Florida, IAPPF reported. That case is separate from the parent company's filing.
  • Goleta, Calif.: This club left the brand in September and became The Grove Pickleball, IAPPF reported.

The St. Louis Business Journal reported that St. Louis investor Richard Chaifetz is a Picklr investor.

Not legal advice. This article summarizes public court records and news reports. If you have a membership, prepayment or other claim, read the official notices on the claims agent's site or talk to a lawyer.

items.title: MLP Nations Cup preview: eight teams, rosters and how to watch, Oct. 30-Nov. 1
items.desc: Preview of the first MLP Nations Cup at Brookhaven Country Club: dates, format, all eight rosters, Tama Shimabukuro replacing Hien Truong on Asia International, schedule, streaming and tickets.
items.body:
Major League Pickleball's first Nations Cup starts Friday, Oct. 30. Eight regional teams will play through Sunday, Nov. 1, at Brookhaven Country Club in the Dallas area, MLP announced. MLP calls the event the official kickoff to the 2026 Pickleball World Championships.

Venue and format

The official World Championships event page gives the venue as Brookhaven Country Club, 3334 Golfing Green Drive, Farmers Branch, Texas. It says Worlds week is played on the same campus. The event uses MLP's coed team format.

Friday and Saturday are round-robin play within two groups of four. On Sunday, the official schedule says the top two teams from each group advance to a single-elimination bracket, and the winner becomes the first Nations Cup champion. Sunday's semifinals are set for 10 a.m. (Group A No. 2 vs. Group B No. 1) and 11:30 a.m. (Group A No. 1 vs. Group B No. 2) Central time, with the final at 2 p.m.

Group A

From MLP's roster announcement:

  • USA: Tyra Black, Anna Bright, Kate Fahey, Ben Johns, CJ Klinger, Will Howells. Captain Johnny Goldberg. MLP repeated the lineup on X.
  • Canada: Victoria DiMuzio, Blaine Hovenier, Armaan Jiwa Mawji, Layne Sleeth, Ryan Torresin, Angie Walker. Captain Steve Deakin.
  • Asia Domestic: Augie Ge (China), Milan Rane (India), Jonathan Truong (Vietnam), Zoey Wang (Chinese Taipei), Jamie Wei (Chinese Taipei), Len Yang (China). Captains Geoffrey Nguyen and Jeff Tsao.
  • Europe-West: Judit Castillo (Spain), Helena Jansen (Spain), Will MacKinnon (Scotland), Theo Platel (France), Estee Widdershoven (Belgium), DJ Young (Spain). Captain Chris Cantino.

Group B

  • Asia International: Rika Fujiwara (Japan), Lingwei Kong (China), Jimmy Liong (Malaysia), Tama Shimabukuro, Jack Wong (Hong Kong, China), Macy Ybanez (Philippines). Captain Madeleine Lim.
  • Australia: Sarah Burr, Chris Crouch, Sahra Dennehy, Mitch Hargreaves, Danni-Elle Townsend, George Wall. Captain Sange Carter.
  • Europe-East: Andrei Daescu (Romania), Arwid Dahlin (Sweden), Ivan Jakovljevic (Croatia), Lina Padegimaite (Lithuania), Tina Pisnik (Slovenia), Daria Walczak (Poland). Captain Caleb Garrard.
  • Latin America: Nico Acevedo (Chile), Mari Humberg (Brazil), Rafa Lenhard (Brazil), Eric Oncins (Brazil), Alexa Schull (Puerto Rico), Charlie Trevino (Mexico). Captain Juan Manuel Benitez.

The Asia International change

The Sept. 24 announcement listed Hien Truong (Vietnam) on Asia International. On Oct. 20, MLP posted a roster update on X saying Tama Shimabukuro joins the Asia International squad in place of Truong. MLP did not give a reason for the change in that post.

Opening matches

Play starts at 10 a.m. Central on Friday on Championship Court with Australia vs. Asia International, according to the match schedule. Europe-East vs. Latin America, Europe-West vs. Asia Domestic, Canada vs. USA, Australia vs. Europe-East and Asia Domestic vs. Canada follow. Saturday also starts at 10 a.m. with Latin America vs. Asia International, and the day includes USA vs. Europe-West and USA vs. Asia Domestic.

How to watch and tickets

All matches are available on PickleballTV and the PickleballTV app, MLP said. The Worlds event page says Championship Court matches are livestreamed on PickleballTV. Tickets are sold on Tixr, separately from Worlds week tickets. The event page lists Courtside and VIP passes, and says current prices are on Tixr. Doors open one hour before the first scheduled match each day.
